chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.summary: Why handlers: exceptions are the one algebraic effect whose standard construct (catching) is not an operation, and the paper sets out to generalise that construct to all effects, with semantics as homomorphisms from free models.

chapters.title: 1. Exception Handlers
chapters.summary: Exceptions first: from a simple try/catch to Benton–Kennedy style handling with a success continuation, then the leap to handling arbitrary operations.

chapters.title: 2. Syntax
chapters.summary: The calculus: signatures of operations with parameter and arity types, a call-by-push-value split between value and computation types, terms including handlers and the handling construct, typing rules, and derived forms.

chapters.title: 3. Examples
chapters.summary: Six worked handlers that show the range of the construct beyond exceptions.

chapters.title: 4. Semantics
chapters.summary: Denotational semantics: effect theories (operations plus equations over templates), their interpretation as models, and the meaning of values and computations, with handling as the induced homomorphism.

chapters.title: 5. Reasoning about handlers
chapters.summary: A logic for reasoning about handlers, including when a handler is correct: its operation clauses are defined and respect the equations of the effect theory.

chapters.title: 6. Deciding handler correctness
chapters.summary: How hard it is to check correctness: for simple signatures, deciding correctness of a single handler is Π2-complete, and Σ1-complete for uniformly simple families of handlers.

chapters.title: 7. Recursion
chapters.summary: Adding recursion: models become pointed ω-cpos, free models come from a left adjoint to the forgetful functor, and the standard semantic monads reappear.

chapters.title: Appendix A. Decidability of handler correctness
chapters.summary: The proofs behind the decidability results of Section 6.

title: Handling Algebraic Effects
byline: Gordon D. Plotkin & Matija Pretnar · Logical Methods in Computer Science 9(4:23), 2013 (arXiv:1312.1399)
note: PDF pages match the printed journal pages (1–36). Conclusion, acknowledgments and references are not broken out. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: The paper that turned exception handlers into a general construct for every algebraic effect. Effects are given by operations plus equations (an effect theory); a computation is an element of the free model of that theory, and a handler supplies another model, so handling is the unique homomorphism out of the free model. The authors build this into a call-by-push-value calculus with value and computation types, show handlers for nondeterminism, CCS, I/O, timeout, rollback and stream redirection, give a denotational semantics, and study when a handler is correct (respects the equations): undecidable in general, with exact complexity bounds for simple signatures. A final section adds recursion over ω-cpos.
